info.title: Meridian Settlement API
info.summary: Captures in, payouts out, and a ledger that always balances.
info.description:
The Meridian Settlement API moves money from the moment a payment is captured to the moment it lands in a merchant's bank account.

**Meridian Payments is fictional.** Every endpoint, identifier and amount in this document is invented for demonstration.

## Concepts

- A **capture** is money taken from a payer.
- Captures for one merchant, one currency and one window form a **run**.
- A closed run becomes part of a **payout** to a verified bank account.
- Every movement is written to the **ledger** as balanced double entries.

## Money

Amounts are always integer minor units plus a currency code. The API never accepts or returns a float for money.

get.description: Returns merchant accounts visible to the calling platform key, newest first. Filter by onboarding status to find accounts that still need attention.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only return merchants in this onboarding state.

post.description: Creates a merchant account in the `pending_review` state. Settlement is disabled until the account passes review and at least one verified payout destination exists.

patch.description: Partial update using JSON Merge Patch semantics. Fields set to `null` are cleared; fields left out are kept.

200.description: Every destination on file, verified or not.

post.description: Adds a bank account the merchant can be paid into. A new destination starts `unverified`; Meridian sends two micro-deposits which the merchant confirms.

local.summary: A domestic account and routing number

get.description: The schedule in force today. Historic schedules are kept and referenced by each run line that used them.

put.description: A new schedule takes effect at the start of the next settlement window after `effective_from`; it never changes a run already open.

202.description: Accepted; it will apply from the next window.

post.description: Records funds captured from a cardholder or account holder. A capture joins the merchant's open run for its currency and is settled when that run closes.

200.description: Every refund issued against the capture.

post.description: Refunds all or part of a capture. The sum of refunds can never exceed the captured amount; a request that would is refused with `422` and the remaining refundable amount.

get.description: A run groups every monetary movement for one merchant, one currency and one settlement window. Runs are listed newest window first.

get.summary: List the lines of a run
get.description: Every line that makes up the run's net amount, in the order they were appended. Lines are immutable: a correction is a new line that reverses an earlier one.

post.description: Closes an open run before its window ends, for example ahead of a public holiday. Closing is final: later captures open a new run.

reason.description: Free text kept on the run's audit trail.

200.description: The payout and the runs it settles.

post.description: Stops a scheduled payout from being released. Only payouts in `scheduled` can be held.
Attaches evidence to a dispute. Evidence can be added until `respond_by`; each item is one of the shapes in `Evidence`.
Locks a conversion rate for a short time. A capture that references the quote settles at the locked rate even if the market moves.

get.description: Indicative mid-market rates for every supported pair. Indicative rates are never used to settle; lock a quote for that.
Double-entry postings behind every balance. Each movement writes two or more entries whose amounts sum to zero per currency.

post.description: Builds a report comparing runs, payouts and bank statement lines for a period. Large periods are built asynchronously; poll the returned report.

201.description: The endpoint, with its signing secret shown once.

post.summary: A run closed and its totals are sealed

Identifier.description: A prefixed, URL-safe identifier. The prefix names the object type.

DecimalString.description: A decimal carried as a string so no precision is lost in transit.

Money.description: An amount of money. Always integer minor units plus a currency: never a float.

amount_minor.description: Amount in the currency's minor unit (cents, öre). Negative for debits.

Metadata.description: Up to 20 key-value pairs of your own. Meridian stores them and never reads them.

region.description: State, county or province, where the country uses one.

MerchantStatus.description: `restricted` merchants can capture but are not paid out; `suspended` merchants can do neither.

MerchantCategory.description: What the merchant sells, in Meridian's own coarse categories.

trading_name.description: The name a customer sees on their statement, if different.

capabilities.description: What the account can do right now, after review.

requirements.description: Anything still needed before the account is fully active.

Balance.description: A merchant's position in one currency.

reserved.description: Held back against open disputes and rolling reserves.

SettlementWindow.description: When runs close and how long funds wait before payout.

cutoff_local.description: Local time at which the run closes.

delay_days.description: Business days between a run closing and its payout.

BankAccount.description: Where money is paid. The `scheme` decides which fields apply.

routing_number.description: Bank or branch code, in the country's own format.

masked.description: The account as shown to people: only its last four characters.

default.description: Exactly one verified destination per currency is the default.

FeeSchedule.description: How Meridian's fee is computed on each capture.

tiers.description: Tiers by monthly captured volume; the first tier whose ceiling is not yet reached applies.

fx_margin_bps.description: Margin over mid-market on conversions, in basis points.

minimum_monthly.description: Charged as a top-up line when monthly fees fall short of it.

up_to_volume.description: Ceiling of this tier. `null` for the last, open-ended tier.

PaymentMethod.description: How the payer paid. Only the non-sensitive outline is ever stored or returned.

network.description: Card network (fictional networks in this sample).

underlying.description: The card behind the wallet token, when the wallet discloses it.

fx_quote_id.description: Settle at a locked rate. The quote must not have expired.

reference.description: Your own order or invoice reference.

amount.description: Leave out to refund everything still refundable.

RunState.description: `closing` lasts seconds while the run's totals are sealed; nothing can join a run after it.

id.description: A content hash of the merchant, currency and window, so replaying a window never makes a second run.

sealed_hash.description: SHA-256 over every line, set when the run closes.

RunTotals.description: `net = gross - fees - refunds + adjustments`, always, to the minor unit.

reverses_seq.description: Set when this line corrects an earlier one.

until.description: Release automatically on this date. Leave out to hold until released.

Evidence.description: One item of evidence. Text, a file you uploaded, or a delivery record.

amount.description: Optional: the amount you intend to convert; very large amounts may get a shorter lock.

journal_id.description: Entries sharing a journal balance to zero per currency.

ReconciliationBreak.description: One place where the books and the bank disagree.

secret.description: Returned only when the endpoint is created. Use it to verify the `Meridian-Signature` header.

attempt.description: Delivery attempt; retries back off over 72 hours.

Problem.description: An error, in the problem-details shape.

errors.description: Field-level problems, one per offending field.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: A unique key per logical operation. Replaying the same key and body returns the first result; the same key with a different body is a `409`.

Unauthorized.description: The key is missing, revoked or lacks the scope.

NotFound.description: No object with that identifier is visible to this key.

Conflict.description: An idempotency key was reused with a different body, or the object changed state.

Unprocessable.description: The request was well-formed but breaks a business rule.

TooManyRequests.description: Slow down. Retry after the number of seconds in `Retry-After`.
